title: Introspective FP8 telemetry-led activation and backstop plan for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Amina Patel
description: Goal: Enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles for a curated set of Hopper-backed models via an introspective, telemetry-driven activation pipeline that minimizes customer-visible regressions. This ticket delivers the calibration orchestration, metric gating, and automated backstops (INT8/FP16 fallbacks) required for safe production rollout. Context: multiple prior calibration artifacts exist; this work focuses on operationalizing a telemetry feedback loop that can automatically pause/rollback activations based on signal quality and regression detection. Key constraints: budgeted runtime changes must not increase p50 latency >5% for P99-bound apps, and quality regressions must be detected at cohort level for top-50 production prompts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator runs calibration job and emits canonical telemetry for each candidate profile (per-model, per-shard). 2) Canary population with 1% traffic can be promoted to progressive ramp if no regression triggers for 48h. 3) Automated fallback to INT8 or FP16 occurs when one or more gating rules fire. 4) E2E test harness runs golden prompt suite and compares token-level divergence; must surface human-review alerts when divergence > threshold. 5) All artifacts (calibration outputs, telemetry dashboards, PRs) are linked and reproducible with a single script.
implementation_notes: High-level flow: 1) Calibration runner produces per-layer scaling factors and per-op statistical profiles for E4M3 and E5M2 candidates. 2) Runner uploads artifacts to S3 with signed metadata and fingerprints. 3) Activation orchestrator launches dark traffic shadow canaries that run both FP8 and baseline (FP16/INT8) and collects KPIs. 4) Introspective gate evaluates telemetry buckets (latency, token edit distance surrogate, perplexity drift, numeric instability counts). 5) Promotion policy: pass 3 sequential gating windows at increasing traffic exposure (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%). Implementation details: use existing calibration container (calib-runner:v2), extend it to emit layerwise histograms and integer overflow counters. Add an annotator job that correlates prompts with golden labels for regression sniffing. Use the rollout controller to inject per-route model variants and KV-cache compatibility checks.
telemetry_requirements: Required signals: request_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, tokens_per_request, token_emission_rate, numeric-instability-events (NaN/Inf), kv-cache-mismatch-count, token_edit_distance_estimate, perplexity_delta_vs_baseline, top_k_confidence_shift. Thresholds: p99_latency increase <= 8% for canary, token_edit_distance_estimate median < 0.6 on golden prompts, numeric-instability-events < 1 per 1e6 tokens, kv-cache-mismatch-count must be zero for warmstart scenarios. Telemetry must be available within 1m of request for gating to act in near-real-time.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for calibration runner and histogram emission. 2) Canary test with synthetic workload replicating top-100 prompt shapes. 3) Golden suite: 3K curated prompts representing chat, instruction, summarization, code; run baseline vs FP8 and compute token-level diffs. 4) Downstream functional tests for tool-calling and structured output. 5) Chaos test: inject simulated quantization noise and confirm gatefires. 6) Load test: verify throughput gains and ensure batching behavior doesn't regress tail latency.
rollback_plan: 1) Automatic rollback trigger: any hard gating rule fires (numeric-instability-events exceed threshold OR token_edit_distance_estimate median > threshold OR kv-cache-mismatch detected). 2) Immediate action: switch traffic to pinned baseline model variant (FP16 or INT8 profile) via rollout controller and shadow-stop FP8 variant. 3) Post-rollback: create incident, capture full trace bundle and calibration artifact, run targeted repro on calibration harness, and open follow-up engineering ticket. 4) Human escalation: if rollback repeats across >3 canaries within 72h, pause all FP8 promotions and schedule cross-team postmortem.
decisions: Select E4M3 as primary profile for high-sensitivity layers and E5M2 as fallback candidate for layers with high numeric variance
Telemetry-led gating instead of fixed-time canaries to reduce human ops and speed up failure detection
Require KV-cache compatibility test for any warmstart-enabled route before promotion
Promotion windows: shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated gating checks between windows
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and QA teams. Agreed on golden prompt set ownership (DX owns the initial 3K prompts).
2025-01-22: Prototyped histogram emission in calib-runner:v2; produced per-layer scale reports for a small 7B model.
2025-01-29: Implemented KV-cache mismatch detector; found warmstart mismatch on 2/15 prompts; root cause: cache key hashing difference between FP8 runtime and baseline. Diego assigned to patch.
2025-02-03: Telemetry pipeline added p99 latency and numeric-instability-events metrics to the rollout controller feed. Canary infra ready for dark traffic injection.
2025-02-07: First shadow canary run started with 0.1% shadow traffic for two non-critical routes; no hard gating rules have fired in the initial 24h.
notes_for_reviewers: Primary reviewer should validate gating thresholds and ensure the golden prompt set covers edge-case tokenization issues (emoji, combining diacritics, long-code snippets). Also confirm the patch for KV-cache hashing maintains backward compatibility for existing persisted caches.
next_steps: 1) Complete KV-cache hashing fix and validate against the 3K golden prompts. 2) Run full calibration across medium and large models and publish artifacts. 3) Kick off public canary for a single low-SLA route with 1% traffic. 4) If stable for 72h, expand promotion cadence and prepare release notes.
